paper.title: Global burden of bacterial antimicrobial resistance in 2019: a systematic analysis

thesis: A global model using two counterfactuals bounds the 2019 mortality burden of bacterial antimicrobial resistance while exposing major uncertainty from sparse surveillance data.

nodes.title: What was the global AMR burden in 2019?
nodes.body: Estimate deaths and DALYs associated with and directly attributable to bacterial antimicrobial resistance across countries and pathogen–drug combinations.

nodes.title: Use two counterfactuals
nodes.body: Estimate attributable burden by replacing resistant infection with susceptible infection, and associated burden by replacing it with no infection.

nodes.title: Combine ten estimation steps
nodes.body: Integrate GBD 2019 estimates, surveillance, clinical, microbiology and pharmaceutical data across five modelling components.

nodes.title: Directly attributable deaths
nodes.body: Under the susceptible-infection counterfactual, an estimated 1.27 million deaths were directly attributable to resistance.

nodes.title: Deaths associated with resistance
nodes.body: Under the no-infection counterfactual, 4.95 million deaths were associated with bacterial AMR, including directly attributable deaths.

nodes.title: AMR is a leading global health burden
nodes.body: Both counterfactuals place bacterial AMR among the largest global causes of mortality, with highest rates in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.

nodes.title: Surveillance gaps shape uncertainty
nodes.body: Nineteen of 204 locations had no data for any modelling component; sparse linked outcome data required shared relative-risk assumptions.

nodes.title: Match measure to intervention
nodes.body: Use attributable burden for resistance-focused interventions and associated burden for infection-prevention interventions such as vaccination.

openQuestions: The paper reports substantial country-level data sparsity and model assumptions; point estimates must remain attached to uncertainty intervals and counterfactual definitions.
